image.altEn: Spanish-language xkcd comic #808: The Economic Argument

titleText.en: Not to be confused with 'making money selling this stuff to OTHER people who think it works', which corporate accountants and actuaries have zero problems with.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish source manifest supplies only the truncated title text “No confundir con ”, which is preserved exactly rather than completed from the official English wording. The official English title text is preserved exactly. OCR merged the two words in ¿ES ASÍ?, omitted both checkmarks, read ESTARÍAN without its accent, and split the visibly wrapped MODER-/NO; the authored inventory follows the Spanish raster. GPS is an unchanged initialism and the two checkmarks are symbols, so all three are visible exclusions rather than Spanish word cards.

applications.explanationEn: Disparatado follows fenómeno and describes what kind of phenomenon is meant.
Disparatado uses masculine singular -o to agree with fenómeno.

regions.labelEs: SI FUNCIONARA, LAS EMPRESAS LO ESTARÍAN USANDO PARA PONERSE LAS BOTAS CON...

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces the imagined condition and has no accent when it means “if.”
Funcionara is the -ra hypothetical form inside the imagined condition.
Estarían is the conditional, or “would,” form that begins the imagined result.
Estarían is the plural conditional helper, and usando is the ongoing form ending in -ando.
Para introduces the purpose, and ponerse remains in its unchanged dictionary form with se attached.
Se is attached to the unchanged infinitive poner, forming ponerse.
The three fixed words form the informal expression for profiting greatly in this business context.
The statement order es así remains unchanged; the question marks and spoken intonation turn it into a yes-or-no question.

regions.labelEs: VISIÓN REMOTA · RADIESTESIA · AURAS · HOMEOPATÍA · REZO A DISTANCIA · ASTROLOGÍA · TAROT · ENERGÍA CRISTAL · MALDICIONES O HECHIZOS · RELATIVIDAD · ELECTRODINÁMICA CUÁNTICA

applications.explanationEn: Visión names perception and remota supplies the conventional paranormal term's ‘remote’ description.
Remota follows visión and describes it.
Remota uses feminine singular -a to agree with visión.
A and distancia form the fixed expression describing something done remotely or from far away.
The noun and its description form the conventional Spanish technical name for quantum electrodynamics.
Cuántica follows electrodinámica and classifies which kind is meant.
Cuántica uses feminine singular -a to agree with electrodinámica.

regions.labelEs: BÚSQUEDA DE PETRÓLEO · REDUCCIÓN DE LOS COSTES SANITARIOS · PLANES DE NEGOCIO/FINANCIEROS · ENERGÍA NORMAL · EL EJÉRCITO · DISPOSITIVOS GPS · DISEÑO DE CIRCUITOS DE SEMICONDUCTORES

excludedUnits.rationale: GPS is an unchanged international initialism rather than a Spanish lexical word occurrence.

applications.explanationEn: Búsqueda names the search, de introduces its target, and petróleo names what is being sought.
Sanitarios follows costes and classifies the costs as healthcare-related.
Sanitarios uses masculine plural -os to agree with costes.
Planes supplies the plural head, while de negocio stays together to classify them as business plans.
After the slash, financieros is the alternative description of planes and follows the noun it describes.
Financieros uses masculine plural -os to agree with planes across the printed alternative.
Normal follows energía and describes it as ordinary rather than paranormal.
Normal has one singular form for both genders, so it remains normal with the feminine noun energía.

regions.labelEs: AL FINAL, AFIRMAR QUE ESTAS COSAS FUNCIONAN SIGNIFICA AFIRMAR QUE EL CAPITALISMO MODERNO NO ESTÁ TAN DESPIADADAMENTE ENFOCADO A LOS BENEFICIOS.

applications.explanationEn: Al and final form the fixed connector that frames the conclusion reached after considering the table.
Significa carries the changed present form, while afirmar stays in its unchanged dictionary form as the action that this entails.
Moderno follows capitalismo and describes it.

applications.exampleEs: CAPITALISMO MODERNO NO ESTÁ TAN DESPIADADAMENTE ENFOCADO
applications.explanationEn: Both moderno and enfocado use masculine singular -o because they describe capitalismo; the verb and modifiers simply stand between the noun and the second description.
Despiadada takes the adverb-forming ending -mente to describe the manner of the focus.
Tan goes immediately before the adverb despiadadamente and raises its degree to ‘so ruthlessly.’

applications.exampleEs: ESTÁ TAN DESPIADADAMENTE ENFOCADO A LOS BENEFICIOS
applications.explanationEn: Está and enfocado form the state, tan despiadadamente modifies its intensity and manner, and a los beneficios names the target of that focus.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

example.es: Necesito una mochila nueva.
example.en: I need a new backpack.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.questionEn: What “economic argument” is the comic using, and what makes the table funny?
cards.answerEn: It argues that a genuinely useful phenomenon should attract profit-seeking organizations; the unchecked paranormal claims contrast with accepted physics that already has practical uses.
cards.noteEn: The table pairs each claim with a lucrative or strategic use. Relativity and quantum electrodynamics get checkmarks because they support real technologies, while the claimed paranormal effects do not. This is a skeptical rule of thumb, not a formal proof. The title-text joke adds an important distinction: companies can still profit by selling a belief to customers even when the claimed effect itself does not work.
Disparatado describes an idea or claim that is unreasonable or makes little sense. It changes to disparatada, disparatados, or disparatadas to match what it describes.

example.es: Ese rumor parece disparatado.
example.en: That rumor seems absurd.

cards.questionEn: How do you describe an imagined “if…, …would…” situation?
cards.answerEn: Use si followed by a hypothetical past verb form for the condition, and use a “would” form for the result.
cards.noteEn: Spanish calls the condition's verb form the imperfect subjunctive. It often ends in -ra or -se, as in tuviera or tuviese. The result uses the conditional, often ending in -ría, as in haría. In this pattern, do not put the conditional directly after si.

example.es: Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más.
example.en: If I had time, I would travel more.

cards.noteEn: Funcionara is a hypothetical past form of funcionar. After si, it presents something as imagined rather than stating that it really works.

example.es: Si el plan funcionara, ahorraríamos tiempo.
example.en: If the plan worked, we would save time.

cards.noteEn: Lo replaces a masculine singular thing, or sometimes a whole idea, as the direct object. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.

example.es: Tengo el libro y lo leo.
example.en: I have the book and I’m reading it.

cards.answerEn: would be (helper before an ongoing action)
cards.noteEn: Estarían is the plural “would” form of estar. Before a form ending in -ando or -iendo, it helps describe what people or things would be doing.

example.es: A esta hora estarían trabajando.
example.en: At this time they would be working.

cards.answerEn: Use a form of estar followed by an action word ending in -ando or -iendo.
cards.noteEn: Estar changes to show who is doing the action: estoy, estás, está, and so on. For most verbs, replace -ar with -ando (hablar → hablando) and replace -er or -ir with -iendo (comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo). This is similar to English “am/is/are doing.”
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone is in the middle of doing something?

example.es: Estoy leyendo.
example.en: I am reading.

cards.answerEn: Use para followed by the verb’s dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir and is called the infinitive. Use para + verb when the same person or thing performs both actions: in estudio para aprender, I both study and learn. When someone else performs the second action, Spanish needs the different pattern para que.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “in order to do something” in Spanish?

example.es: Estudio para aprender.
example.en: I study in order to learn.

cards.answerEn: to make a killing; to profit greatly (in ponerse las botas)
cards.noteEn: Ponerse normally means putting something on or entering a state. In the informal expression ponerse las botas, the whole phrase can mean profiting or enjoying something in abundance.

example.es: Los vendedores se pusieron las botas durante la feria.
example.en: The sellers made a killing during the fair.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

example.es: Quiero ayudarte.
example.en: I want to help you.

cards.questionEn: What informal expression can mean making a lot of money or profiting greatly?
cards.answerEn: Use ponerse las botas; in a money context, it means to make a killing or profit handsomely.
cards.noteEn: The literal words refer to putting on boots, but the fixed expression means getting an abundant benefit. The short attached part changes for the person: me pongo, te pones, se pone, nos ponemos, os ponéis, or se ponen las botas.

example.es: Con las ventas de verano, la tienda se puso las botas.
example.en: The shop made a killing on the summer sales.

cards.answerEn: boots; completes ponerse las botas, ‘to make a killing’ here
cards.noteEn: Botas literally means boots. In ponerse las botas, it belongs to an informal fixed expression whose meaning comes from the phrase, not from footwear.

example.es: Con aquel encargo, se pusieron las botas.
example.en: They made a killing on that job.

cards.questionEn: How can Spanish turn an ordinary statement into a yes-or-no question?
cards.answerEn: Use question marks and questioning intonation; Spanish does not need a separate helper like English do or does.
cards.noteEn: The word order can remain the same as in a statement, especially in conversation. The opening and closing question marks show the question in writing.

example.es: ¿Tienen café?
example.en: Do they have coffee?

cards.noteEn: Visión can mean the ability to see, what someone sees, or a broader viewpoint. The written accent marks the stressed final syllable.

example.es: Tiene buena visión de noche.
example.en: She has good night vision.

cards.questionEn: What is the Spanish term for the claimed ability to perceive a distant or hidden target without ordinary senses?
cards.noteEn: Visión names sight or perception, and remota follows it in the feminine form. In paranormal contexts the two-word term refers to a claimed extrasensory ability, not ordinary viewing through a camera.

example.es: El documental examinó la llamada visión remota.
example.en: The documentary examined so-called remote viewing.

cards.noteEn: Remota is the feminine singular form of remoto and matches a feminine noun such as visión.

example.es: La señal viene de una estación remota.
example.en: The signal comes from a remote station.

cards.noteEn: Radiestesia is the claimed practice of finding hidden water, minerals, or other things with a rod, pendulum, or similar object.

example.es: El artículo examinó la radiestesia.
example.en: The article examined dowsing.

cards.noteEn: In mystical claims, an aura is an invisible field said to surround a person or object. The ordinary word can also mean an atmosphere or impression.

example.es: La curandera afirmó que podía ver auras.
example.en: The healer claimed that she could see auras.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a distancia, ‘remotely’ or ‘at a distance’
cards.noteEn: Keep a with distancia in the fixed expression a distancia. It can describe something done from far away or without being physically present.

example.es: La entrevista se hizo a distancia.
example.en: The interview was conducted remotely.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something happens remotely or from far away?
cards.answerEn: Use a distancia after the activity or thing being described.
cards.noteEn: Keep a and distancia together, normally without an article between them. The expression can mean physically “at a distance” or, for work and communication, “remotely.”

example.es: Marta trabaja a distancia tres días por semana.
example.en: Marta works remotely three days a week.

cards.answerEn: crystal; a crystal used in mystical claims
cards.noteEn: Here cristal names the mineral object associated with claims about ‘crystal energy,’ not ordinary window glass. Spanish often makes the relationship explicit with de, as in energía de los cristales.

example.es: La tienda vende cristales decorativos.
example.en: The shop sells decorative crystals.

cards.questionEn: What is the Spanish name for the quantum theory of light and electrically charged particles?
cards.noteEn: Electrodinámica is a feminine noun, so cuántica takes the feminine singular ending -a. This is the conventional technical name, often abbreviated QED in English.

example.es: La electrodinámica cuántica hace predicciones muy precisas.
example.en: Quantum electrodynamics makes very precise predictions.

cards.answerEn: quantum; relating to quantum physics (feminine singular)
cards.noteEn: Cuántica describes a feminine singular noun in the context of quantum physics. The masculine singular form is cuántico.

example.es: Estudian la física cuántica.
example.en: They study quantum physics.

cards.promptEs: búsqueda de + persona, cosa u objetivo
cards.questionEn: What word follows búsqueda before the person, thing, or goal being sought?
cards.answerEn: Use búsqueda de, then name what the search is for.
cards.noteEn: Búsqueda is the noun “search” or “pursuit,” related to the verb buscar. The de remains in the expression while the article and following noun change to fit what is being sought.

example.es: Sigue la búsqueda de una solución.
example.en: The search for a solution continues.

cards.answerEn: for; introduces what a search or pursuit seeks
cards.noteEn: After búsqueda, Spanish uses de before the person, thing, or goal being sought. Natural English usually says “search for,” so the preposition changes between the two languages.

example.es: Continúa la búsqueda de una respuesta.
example.en: The search for an answer continues.

cards.noteEn: Costes is especially common in Spain. Many other regions use costos for the same meaning.

example.es: Tenemos que reducir los costes.
example.en: We have to reduce costs.

cards.noteEn: After costes, sanitarios means costs connected with healthcare. In other contexts, sanitario can refer to sanitation or a healthcare worker.

example.es: El informe compara los gastos sanitarios.
example.en: The report compares healthcare expenses.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “business plan” in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Use plan de negocio; its plural is planes de negocio.
cards.noteEn: De negocio classifies what kind of plan it is. Plan changes to planes in the plural, while de negocio stays unchanged.

example.es: Necesitamos un plan de negocio claro.
example.en: We need a clear business plan.

cards.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’

example.es: Necesito una taza de café.
example.en: I need a coffee cup.

cards.noteEn: In plan de negocio, de negocio classifies the plan as a business plan.

example.es: Prepararon un plan de negocio sencillo.
example.en: They prepared a simple business plan.

cards.noteEn: Dispositivos is the masculine plural of dispositivo, a device or piece of equipment designed for a purpose.

example.es: Apaga los dispositivos electrónicos.
example.en: Turn off the electronic devices.

cards.answerEn: in the; part of al final (“in the end”)

cards.questionEn: How do you say “in the end” or “eventually”?
cards.noteEn: Al final can name the literal end of something or the eventual outcome after events have unfolded.

example.es: Al final, decidimos quedarnos.
example.en: In the end, we decided to stay.

cards.noteEn: Afirmar can mean stating something confidently as true. It does not by itself say whether the claim is correct.

example.es: No basta con afirmar que funciona.
example.en: It is not enough to claim that it works.

cards.noteEn: Que introduces a clause after verbs such as creer, saber, esperar, or decir. English often uses “that,” but may leave it unstated.

example.es: Creo que Ana viene.
example.en: I think that Ana is coming.

cards.noteEn: Funcionan is the present-time plural form of funcionar.

example.es: Estas máquinas funcionan bien.
example.en: These machines work well.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something means doing an action?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of significar followed by the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The plus sign means “followed by.” The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Spanish uses that unchanged form where English often uses an -ing form after “mean.”

example.es: Ser voluntario significa ayudar.
example.en: Being a volunteer means helping.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something is focused on or aimed at a particular goal or audience?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of estar, then enfocado, enfocada, enfocados, or enfocadas, followed by a and the target.
cards.noteEn: Estar changes for the person, thing, and time. Enfocado changes to match what is being described, and a introduces the aim, audience, or intended result. A describing adverb can go before enfocado, as in muy enfocado.

example.es: El proyecto está enfocado a reducir residuos.
example.en: The project is aimed at reducing waste.

cards.questionEn: How do you intensify a describing word to mean “so,” as in “so difficult”?
cards.answerEn: Put tan immediately before the word that describes the person, thing, or action.
cards.noteEn: Tan does not change form. It goes before an adjective, a word that describes a person or thing, or before an adverb, a word that describes an action. Use forms of tanto instead before a noun or when saying “so much” or “so many.”

example.es: El examen fue tan difícil.
example.en: The exam was so difficult.

cards.noteEn: Despiadadamente is built from despiadada, “ruthless,” plus -mente. It describes how an action or focus is pursued.

example.es: La empresa compitió despiadadamente.
example.en: The company competed ruthlessly.

cards.questionEn: How do you turn many describing words into words such as “quickly,” “clearly,” or “probably”?
cards.answerEn: Use the feminine singular form of the describing word and add -mente. If its masculine and feminine forms are identical, simply add -mente.
cards.noteEn: For an adjective that changes, use its -a form: claro becomes clara and then claramente. For one form shared by both genders, probable becomes probablemente. The new word usually describes how an action happens or how the speaker judges a claim.

example.es: Lucía responde claramente.
example.en: Lucía answers clearly.

cards.noteEn: Enfocado describes something directed toward a subject, goal, or result. It changes to enfocada, enfocados, or enfocadas to match what is described.

example.es: El curso está enfocado a principiantes.
example.en: The course is aimed at beginners.

cards.answerEn: at; toward; introduces the target after enfocado
cards.noteEn: After enfocado or enfocada, a can introduce the audience, goal, or result that something is aimed at.

example.es: La campaña está enfocada a los jóvenes.
example.en: The campaign is aimed at young people.

cards.noteEn: In business and economics, beneficios commonly means the money left as profit, not merely general advantages.

example.es: La compañía declaró beneficios este año.
example.en: The company reported profits this year.
